text:
alex.p: Heads-up — tenant-54 backups started failing decrypt in prod right after the rollback at 08:12. Getting AccessDenied from KMS when restoring snapshots.
jamie: Ugh. Which key? full error?
alex.p: Error in restore job: 
```
DecryptError: AccessDenied: User: arn:aws:sts::111122223333:assumed-role/backup-uploader/xyz is not authorized to use key arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:111122223333:key/abcd-ef01
```
olivia.s: cc @ryan-oncall — this looks like the CMK grant for the backup-uploader principal was removed during the RBAC rollback. I see an admin role change in the audit log at 08:10.
ryan-oncall: I saw the alert from sec-bot earlier. Investigating now. Can someone paste the audit log entry id?
alex.p: log id `audit-08a3b7` — shows `iam:PutRolePolicy` by service-account:infra-ops with summary "revert: tenant-role-cleanup".
sec-bot: Automated detection: KMS GrantDeleted for key/abcd-ef01 at 08:09:58 by infra-ops svc-account. Possible impact: snapshot restores and scheduled backups for tenants using CMK.
jamie: Okay — immediate plan: 1) confirm the grant removal 2) re-create a minimal grant for backup-uploader role with least privilege 3) re-run the restore job as a canary.
olivia.s: Agreed. Also we need to add a guard in the RBAC rollback playbook to check for CMK grants referencing deleted roles. Right now it only checks IAM role names.
ryan-oncall: Recreated a temporary grant pointing to `arn:aws:iam::111122223333:role/backup-uploader` with Encrypt/Decrypt for 1 hour — re-run restore?
alex.p: Re-run started — still failing with same AccessDenied.
jamie: Did we use the correct grant principal? The restore runs as an assumed-role session (`assumed-role/backup-uploader/restore-session`). The grant principal should be the role ARN (not the assumed one) — but kms accepts role ARNs. Can you paste the grant principal string?
ryan-oncall: Grant principal: `arn:aws:iam::111122223333:role/backup-uploader`. Looks right.
olivia.s: Check key policy too — if the key policy was replaced during rotation/rollback it could lock out grants. Run `aws kms get-key-policy --key-id abcd-ef01 --policy-name default` and search for `backup-uploader`.
jamie: I pulled the key policy — it only lists admin principals now, not the backup role. That would supersede the grant. Someone must have overwritten the key policy during the rollback.
sec-bot: Recent api events: `KMS:PutKeyPolicy` by infra-ops svc-account at 08:09:55. Diff: removed `backup-uploader` entry.
alex.p: Great catch. So we need to restore key policy + grant. Two options: 1) roll forward key policy to include backup-uploader (fast) 2) create a short-lived KMS external user mapping for restore (riskier). I'd vote for 1.
ryan-oncall: I'm restoring the previous key policy from backup (policy snapshot `kp-2026-03-20-22:00`) and will reattach minimal grant.
jamie: Make sure you document the exact policy version and record the audit id for the remediation. Also note we should alert compliance — this touched tenant data.
olivia.s: Compliance pinged. They want a timeline and a list of affected snapshots and tenants. I can run a query against the snapshot metadata table to find blobs referencing key `abcd-ef01`. Running: `SELECT snapshot_id, tenant FROM snapshots WHERE kms_key = 'arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:111122223333:key/abcd-ef01'`
alex.p: We have ~24 snapshots across 3 tenants. Tenant-54 is the one that tried restore.
ryan-oncall: Restored key policy and added grant. Re-run restore — job returned success now. :thumbsup:
jamie: Nice. Post-mortem items (short): - Add pre-rollback checklist to detect KMS key deps - Prevent infra-ops rollback from applying key policy diffs without at least 2 approvals for keys in prod - Add alert for `KMS:PutKeyPolicy` in prod with high severity - Add a canary suite that attempts a decrypt after infra changes
olivia.s: Also need to fix audit logging correlation: infra-ops used a machine user svc-account that isn't tied to a person. We need owner tags and 2FA on that service credential.
sec-bot: Recommended ticket template created: SECURITY-ENC-2345. Include timeline, snapshots affected, audit diffs, and the remediation steps.
alex.p: Can we add a safety check to the rollback tooling that scans for KMS principals referenced by role names about to be deleted? If a match is found, block and require explicit ack.
jamie: Yeah, we can add `scripts/check_kms_policy_refs.sh` as a preflight. Example check: `aws kms list-key-policies --key-id $KEY | xargs -I{} aws kms get-key-policy --key-id $KEY --policy-name {} | grep -E "$ROLE_NAME"` — fail if found.
ryan-oncall: I'll open a PR to add that to the rollback playbook and to modify the infra CI to require `kms-ack` label for the PR.
olivia.s: For immediate compliance deliverables I'm attaching the list of snapshots and the time window (08:05-08:12) when the policy change happened. Also adding a note that tenant data was not exfiltrated.
alex.p: Thanks all. Action owners: ry an-oncall — remediation + PR; jamie — alert and postmortem; olivia — compliance report; alex — follow-up on svc-account credential lockdown. We'll update this thread when PRs are merged.
ryan-oncall: PR opened: infra#4126 with check and kms-ack gating.
jamie: Filing the postmortem doc now. WIll link shortly. :spiral_notepad:
sec-bot: Closing monitoring loop: all restores green, no further decrypt errors. Continuing to watch for KMS:PutKeyPolicy events with elevated alerting.
alex.p: Good work. We'll schedule a quick drill next week to run a simulated rollback and ensure the preflight catches this.
